benchmark_gaps: TSP Christofides uses greedy matching instead of Edmonds' blossom algorithm, so the 1.5-approximation guarantee does not hold; measured max ratio 1.057 at n=10 on random Euclidean instances (n=8: 1.045)
TSP nearest-neighbor has no approximation guarantee; measured max ratio 1.055 at n=10 (n=8: 1.000 — NN found optimal on that instance)
TSP NN + 2-opt reaches ratio 1.0 at n=8 and n=10 on random Euclidean instances, but 2-opt is not integrated into TSPSolver for Christofides or multi_start_nn initial tours
TSP 3-opt reaches ratio 1.0 at n=8 and n=10 but is O(n^3) per iteration and not integrated into TSPSolver.solve()
TSP Lin-Kernighan reaches ratio 1.0 at n=8 but only 1.055 at n=10 (LK did not improve on the NN tour for that instance); LK is not integrated into TSPSolver
TSP Simulated Annealing with 2000 iterations reaches ratio 1.0 at n=8 but degrades to 1.217 at n=10; SA is not integrated into TSPSolver and has no candidate list
VRP Clarke-Wright savings is the only algorithm; no intra-route 2-opt, inter-route relocate/exchange, or ALNS post-processing is applied
VRP has no metaheuristic improvement (SA, GA, ACO, ALNS); solution quality degrades significantly for larger instances
No standard TSP/VRP benchmark instances (TSPLIB, CVRPLIB) are used for validation; only random Euclidean instances are tested
No Held-Karp exact solver integration into TSPSolver for benchmarking heuristic quality on small instances (n <= 15)
bottlenecks: GPUFallback class exists but is never used by any solver; GPU solvers (GPUTSPSolver, GPUVRPSolver) have no try/except fallback to CPU on CUDA failure
GPUTSPSolver._gpu_two_opt evaluates all O(n^2) moves per iteration on GPU but applies only the best one; no parallel move application or candidate list strategy
GPUVRPSolver computes savings on GPU but route merging is sequential on CPU; no GPU-accelerated route improvement
TSPSolver.solve() with improve=True runs 2-opt as a separate pass only for NN and multi_start_nn; Christofides tours are not improved
ThreeOpt is O(n^3) per iteration with no don't-look bits or candidate lists; impractical for n > 200
SimulatedAnnealingTSP uses random 2-opt moves with no candidate list or adaptive neighborhood; convergence is slow for large instances
VRP solver has no post-processing pipeline; savings output is final with no improvement pass
No unified solver interface; users must choose between CPU/GPU, TSP/VRP, and construction/local-search/metaheuristic manually
GPUTSPSolver.solve_batch() processes instances sequentially; no true batched GPU parallelism across instances
No support for time windows (VRPTW), multi-depot VRP, or heterogeneous fleet in any solver
TSPSolver only supports christofides, nearest_neighbor, and multi_start_nn; no SA, LK, or 3-opt integration
VRPSolver only supports savings; no sweep, insertion, or metaheuristic construction
missing_algorithms: Edmonds' blossom algorithm — optimal minimum-weight perfect matching for Christofides; required for the 1.5-approximation guarantee
Or-opt — relocates segments of 1-3 consecutive cities; complements 2-opt by exploring a different neighborhood
Genetic Algorithm for TSP — population-based metaheuristic with crossover (OX, PMX, CX) and mutation; effective for large instances
Ant Colony Optimization for TSP — pheromone-based constructive metaheuristic; strong empirical performance on TSP benchmarks
Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) for VRP — destroy/repair metaheuristic with adaptive operator selection; state-of-the-art for VRP
Sweep algorithm for VRP — simple construction heuristic sorting customers by polar angle from depot
VRPTW support — time window constraints for agricultural operations (e.g., pesticide application windows)
Multi-depot VRP — large farms with multiple depots (e.g., north/south storage)
Heterogeneous fleet VRP — vehicles with different capacities (e.g., drones + tractors)
Intra-route 2-opt and 3-opt for VRP — improve individual routes after savings construction
Inter-route relocate and exchange for VRP — move or swap customers between routes to reduce total cost
Asymmetric TSP (ATSP) support — real-world agricultural routing may have asymmetric distances (one-way fields, elevation)
Christofides + 2-opt/3-opt/LK integration — TSPSolver should offer improve=True for all construction algorithms, not just NN
Unified solver interface — common base class or protocol for CPU/GPU, TSP/VRP, and construction/local-search/metaheuristic
